study: Capsule Review — corrected Galar v2 training-pool label audit
scientific_question: Which as-yet-uninspected permitted fitting examinations can diversify blood-positive examination support, particularly short contiguous annotation runs, without examining reserved evaluation cases?

data_source.attribution: Le Floch et al., Galar, 2025; CC BY 4.0

forbidden_label_reads_in_this_audit: 1-20 and 61-80; inner ZIP metadata may be inspected only to enumerate entries

label_policy.short_run_definition: 1–25 consecutive positive annotated rows at source-frame stride 5; not a verified distinct lesion
label_policy.validation: exactly one selected CSV per exam; expected columns; ordered unique nonnegative source frame IDs; binary/missing values; reject ambiguity and corruption

reported_metrics: all 40 training-candidate examination label supports; including negative and missing studies
per-examination annotated row and primary blood-positive row totals
number and length distribution of blood-positive annotation runs (not lesions)
by-archive group positive-examination counts and known official source sizes
explicit report of missing/unresolved exam-30 source-image mapping
selection_rule: Only use these fitting-pool labels to prioritize later image acquisition. Report all archive-group results rather than selecting a success-looking group silently. Prefer an affordable group with >=3 distinct blood-positive examinations and >=2 examinations with at least one short blood-positive annotation run. If no group meets those conditions, report that; do not relabel future evaluation cases as training. No archive is authorized for download by this audit.
execution_limits: Label-only offline analysis on existing corrected source archive; no image, new model fit, remote compute, clinical review or outcome-based selection on evaluation cases.
artifact_policy: Commit frozen spec, aggregate summary, code and tests only. No per-frame labels, filenames/identity manifests, imagery, weights, or reserved-evaluation measurements.
interpretation: Training-pool feasibility, not independent test performance. Study ID is not confirmed unique patient ID. Blood annotation != diagnosed lesion. The earlier 9-10 development metrics are not newly blinded.
